---
title: "enrichVolcano: rationale & intent"
---

This site documents **why** each `enrichVolcano` function exists, the method it
implements, the defaults it ships with, and the literature those choices rest
on. It complements the reference (`?function`) and the how-to vignettes — here
the focus is *rationale and intent*, not argument-by-argument syntax.

## The pipeline at a glance

`enrich_volcano()` is the hero function. It chains the steps below; each is also
exported so you can run, inspect, or swap any stage.

```
ev_read_contrasts ─▶ ev_validate ─▶ pi_score ─▶ adjust_p ─▶ ev_enrich ─▶ ev_collapse ─▶ ev_volcano_ring ─▶ wrap_plots
   (read CSVs)       (canonicalise)  (Xiao π)   (FDR)       (fgsea/ORA)   (dedup)       (volcano+ring)     (layout*)
```

*`enrich_volcano()` lays panels out with `patchwork::wrap_plots()` directly;
`ev_compose()` is the exported standalone equivalent for assembling
volcano + ring lists yourself.

| Stage | Function | What it decides | Key reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read | `ev_read_contrasts` | per-contrast CSV → long tibble | — |
| Canonicalise | `ev_validate` | detect input format, map IDs | — |
| Score | `pi_score` | combine p-value + effect size | Xiao 2014 |
| Adjust | `adjust_p` | multiple-testing correction | Benjamini–Hochberg 1995 |
| Enrich | `ev_enrich` | ranked GSEA / ORA, **ranked by moderated t** | Subramanian 2005; Korotkevich 2021 |
| Dedup | `ev_collapse` | collapse redundant pathways | Korotkevich 2021; Merico 2010 |
| Plot | `ev_volcano`, `ring_plot`, `ev_volcano_ring` | volcano + enrichment ring | — |
| Compose | `ev_compose` | multi-contrast layout | — |

## Two design commitments

1. **Signed test statistic for GSEA.** Ranking defaults to the limma/proteoDA
   **moderated t-statistic** (`rank_by = "t"`), the recommended signed statistic
   for moderated linear models, falling back to `sign(logFC)·−log10(p)` when no
   `t` column is present. See [methods](methods.qmd#ranking) and
   [`ev_enrich`](functions/ev_enrich.qmd).

2. **Collection-agnostic dedup.** Redundant-pathway collapse uses only
   gene-overlap and ranked-statistic methods that work for *any* gene-set
   collection (Hallmark, Reactome, KEGG, MitoCarta, CORUM, GO). GO-semantic
   methods (`clusterProfiler::simplify`, `rrvgo`) are intentionally **not** core,
   because they require GO structure + an OrgDb. See
   [methods](methods.qmd#deduplication) and [`ev_collapse`](functions/ev_collapse.qmd).
